outcome.technical: Only tests/test_drive_phase.py changed. (1) fx4 (_template_reuse_case, sb-block): wraps _build_repo, calls _repo twice with a gate no other fixture names; asserts the template table grows by one then not at all, the build runs once, and both copies commit one tree. (2) hr3: tied now carries the action; asserts tied[0][2] == TASK_REOPEN and tied[1][2] == RISK_CONFIRMED, so a fixture whose file order flipped can no longer pass on the reading the case refuses. (3) hr13/hr14 in _same_moment_handback_cases: a human re-open a second after the hand-back prints "the newest re-open of it is a re-open for 'the human wants...'"; a journal with no re-open prints "...is absent from the journal"; each excludes the other wordings. (4) _git_bound_names now returns {scope: names} per module/function/lambda/class: locals and parameters hide outer names, class-body names are not seen by methods, bindings follow assignment chains inside a scope; bare_git_calls reads each call against its own scope's set. It reuses the file's existing _scope_nodes (the tuple became _NAME_SCOPES; docstring says every node belongs to exactly one scope). fg2 pins it: twin reports [4, 11]; the module-wide reading reports 8, 16, 18 too. The scan over tests/ still reports {}; wide and fg1m twins unchanged ([2, 4, 5, 7, 10], [1, 2]). (5) _needs_process docstring says it does not detect a case that needs a dead lock holder; the block comment above it no longer implies _needs_process routes such a case. (6) ta9 REPRODUCED, CAUSE FOUND, NOT FIXED (out of scope): the helper at HEAD 8f896d6f printed `red-first: red (throwaway at HEAD 8f896d6f5d30, removed: yes)` and redFirst could-not-prove, `failing cases ta9 (house FAIL), but HEAD's own tests on HEAD's code are not green (SELFTEST FAILED: 788/789 cases passed)`. Cause, in the PRODUCT: drive-phase.py remove_task_tree (the `its marker does not name %s (%s)` return, about line 5186) clips read_provenance's basis to 200 bytes, and that basis opens with the marker file's absolute path (<fixture root>/.git/worktrees/P1.1/audit-worktree.json). Under the throwaway the sweep's TMPDIR is nested several directories deeper, so the clip falls before "for task 'P1.9'" and the did-line loses the task the marker names, which is the fact ta9 asserts. Reproduced by hand: the ta block under a long TMPDIR prints `FAIL ta9 ... (its marker does not name P1.1 (<long path>/bbbbbbbb...))`, 27/28. The test is right; the product is wrong on any machine with a long temp or project path. Proposed fix (<scratchpad>/p15514/product-fix.py, applied ONLY to a scratch copy): name the marker's own taskId before the clipped basis - `its marker names P1.9, not P1.1 (<basis>)`, falling back to the old wording when the record names no task or names this one. Probe row ta9-head FAIL, ta9-fixed PASS (28/28) under the same long TMPDIR. drive-phase.py is not in this task's files and the orchestrator said to edit only declared files in the checkout, so it was not edited and the helper proof after the fix (acceptance 6) is still owed. Gate: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py tools/_suite.py` exit 0, `3/3 files ok, 1192 cases`; drive suite 793 cases (HEAD's ran 789 inside the helper's throwaway). ruff check and vermin -t=3.8- on the suite: exit 0. Dependants: tests/test_drive_phase.py's dependants are still correct: no stage label added or renamed (sweep-costs.json, ci.yml, affected.py, reach-diff.py, test__runner_output.py, test_run_test_gate.py, test_stamp_verification.py and drive-phase.py name the file or its labels, not the edited helpers); _actions/_bindings/_counting/_follower_cases are untouched; _git_bound_names, bare_git_calls and _scope_nodes have no readers outside this file (repo-wide grep). stamp-verification.py, tests/test_stamp_verification.py and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md are unchanged; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md names none of the edited helpers (grep), so nothing needs updating there.
